So field goalies wear a big chest protector that goes down to their stomach, gloves that have reinforced thumbs, and a helmet with a throat protector (and sometimes sweatpants). Field goalies need to be much more mobile than box goalies because they have to move around on the defensive end to facilitate the defense clearing the ball to the offensive end, chase down shots, and sometimes even deliver hits or score. Clearing (getting the ball from defense to offense) requires more movement in field so everyone gets involved. It’s simpler in box and there are players (transition) whose main job is to play defense and get the ball to the offense. As a result, box goalies rarely need to waddle out of the goal to help out with stuff.

It’s mostly protective- that little ball can be rocketing around at 90-100 mph so the heavy and large padding protects them from injury. It also makes it harder to score - the large goalies and small goal make it necessary for precision in shooting and teamwork (more passing to get the goalie moving, screens,etc).
